newsitem.title: UGANDA: Drought forces Uganda March inflation up to 8.5pct.
newsitem.headline: Drought forces Uganda March inflation up to 8.5pct.

text.p: Uganda's annualised headline inflation rose to 8.5 percent in March from 4.9 percent in February on a rise in food prices influenced by drought, the central Bank of Uganda (BOU) said on Wednesday.

"The rise in inflation was due to a sharp rise in prices of staple foods owing to the prolonged drought. Drought struck Uganda's northern and eastern regions since the latter part of last year and only late last month did some rains come," the bank said in a report for March.

The bank said annual underlying inflation, which ignores the fluctuations in food prices, rose to 3.8 percent from 3.2 percent. It said increases were seen in the prices of food, beverages and tobacco, and household and personal goods.

The bank said interest rates continued to decline on government treasury bills. The end-March rates for the 91-, 180-, 273- and 364-day treasury bills stood at 9.86 percent, 13.14 percent, 13.65 percent and 13.75 percent.
This compared with 10.71 percent, 13.62 percent, 14.13 percent and 14.13 percent at end-February.

The total sales of treasury bills in March amounted to 22.38 billion shillings while maturities totalled 16.26 billion. The stock of outstanding bills increased to 78.47 billion shillings in March from 77.34 billion shillings at end-February.
BOU said the bank rate and the rediscount rate also dropped to 14.90 percent and 12.29 percent respectively at end-March compared to 15.10 and 12.90 percent at end-February.
The bank said Uganda's industrial production rose by 11.2 percent in December 1996, with increases registered in production of beer, sugar, soft drinks and cigarretes.
It reported a 31.4 percent decline in textiles production and blamed that on a shortage of raw materials. The bank did not provide actual production figures.
